To convert your grade to a percentage, choose the method below that matches the type of grade you have. 

If you want me to do the math for you, just **type your numbers (e.g., "43 out of 50" or "GPA of 3.4") in a reply**, and I will calculate it instantly!

---

### 1. Point-Based Grade to Percentage (Most Common)
If you have a score like **"43 out of 50"**, use this simple formula:

$$\text{Percentage (\%)} = \left( \frac{\text{Points Earned}}{\text{Total Possible Points}} \right) \times 100$$

* **Example:** If you scored **35 out of 40** points:
  $$\left( \frac{35}{40} \right) \times 100 = 0.875 \times 100 = 87.5\%$$

---

### 2. Letter Grade to Percentage Chart
This is the standard US high school and college grading scale. Note that some schools may have slightly different percentage brackets.

| Letter Grade | Percentage Range | GPA (4.0 Scale) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **A+** | 97% – 100% | 4.0 |
| **A** | 93% – 96% | 4.0 |
| **A-** | 90% – 92% | 3.7 |
| **B+** | 87% – 89% | 3.3 |
| **B** | 83% – 86% | 3.0 |
| **B-** | 80% – 82% | 2.7 |
| **C+** | 77% – 79% | 2.3 |
| **C** | 73% – 76% | 2.0 |
| **C-** | 70% – 72% | 1.7 |
| **D+** | 67% – 69% | 1.3 |
| **D** | 65% – 66% | 1.0 |
| **F** | Below 65% | 0.0 |

---

### 3. GPA (4.0 Scale) to Percentage
Because different schools use different conversions, there is no single "official" formula. However, a widely accepted standard formula to estimate percentage from a 4.0 GPA is:

$$\text{Percentage (\%)} = (\text{GPA} \times 20) + 20$$

* **Example:** If you have a **3.5 GPA**:
  $$(3.5 \times 20) + 20 = 70 + 20 = 90\%$$

---

**Want me to calculate it?** 
Reply with your **points** (e.g., "18 out of 25"), your **letter grade**, or your **GPA**, and I'll give you the percentage right away!
